purpose: Standard sequence for assessing and stabilizing a critically ill or injured patient: treat life-threatening problems before moving to the next letter, and reassess continuously.

sequence.name: Airway
sequence.action: Look for airway obstruction (paradoxical chest movement, accessory muscle use, cyanosis, noisy breathing). Get expert help immediately if obstructed; use positioning, suction, or an airway adjunct; give high-concentration oxygen.

sequence.name: Breathing
sequence.action: Count respiratory rate (normal 12-20/min; >25/min is concerning), assess effort/symmetry, auscultate and percuss the chest, check SpO2. Give oxygen to all critically ill patients; consider bag-mask or non-invasive ventilation if breathing is inadequate.

sequence.name: Circulation
sequence.action: Check skin colour/temperature, capillary refill (normal <2 sec), pulse rate/quality, blood pressure; look for external and concealed bleeding. Insert large-bore IV access, send bloods, give a fluid bolus if hypotensive, and control any hemorrhage.

sequence.name: Disability
sequence.action: Only after A, B, C are addressed: check pupils, assess conscious level (ACVPU or GCS), and check blood glucose. Treat reversible causes (e.g. naloxone for opioid toxicity, glucose for hypoglycemia).

sequence.name: Exposure
sequence.action: Fully expose the patient to look for injuries or rashes while preserving dignity and preventing heat loss.

rule: Treat life-threatening problems at each step before moving to the next. Reassess from A if the patient deteriorates. Call for expert help early and communicate findings clearly (e.g. SBAR).

_sources.title: The ABCDE Approach - Resuscitation Council UK
